paper_metadata.title: Arline Benchmarks: Automated Benchmarking Platform for Quantum Compilers

summary: The paper introduces the Arline Benchmarks platform for automated evaluation of quantum compiler pipelines (Qiskit, Pytket, Cirq, PyZX) using structured and random circuits including VQE (4–12 qubits), TFIM simulation (10–20 qubits), option pricing (11 qubits), and Grover search (9–15 qubits). Experiments analyze metrics such as two‑qubit gate count, circuit depth, and a hardware‑aware cost function across several hardware connectivity models (IBM, Rigetti, IonQ, Google). Results show that compiler performance strongly depends on circuit class, and composite pipelines combining passes from multiple frameworks can reduce CX counts further than individual compilers.
